newsitem.title: USA: Ex-Fed Blinder not returning to Washington...now.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Fed Blinder not returning to Washington...now.

text.p: Alan Blinder, former vice chairman of the Federal Reserve Board, said on Friday he had turned down the Clinton administration's offer to head the Council of Economic Advisers, but is not ruling out taking an official position in the future.

"I'm not going back to Washington. I'm not saying not ever, but not now," Blinder told Reuters upon returning home from Washington where he met with President Clinton on Thursday to discuss his possible appointment as chairman of the CEA.
Blinder declined to explain why he turned down the position or what other positions, if any, he would consider.
"No, that was my answer," added Blinder who has chaired the economics department at Princeton University since leaving the Fed in January.
Joseph Stiglitz, current chairman of the CEA, has announced he is leaving the position to become chief economist at the World Bank.
Blinder served as a member of the CEA in 1993 to mid 1994 and served as Vice Chairman of the Federal Reserve Bank between July 1994 and Janmuary 1996.
